name: Quantum Circuit Vision
reason: arXiv:2607.10057 (v1, 2026-07-11) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('Quantum Circuit Vision: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Visual AI Agents for Quantum Code Generation', Liu/Zhang/Zhang, AWS + Duke Kunshan). QCV-Dataset verified on Hugging Face (QuantBlockchain/qcv-dataset, MIT, quantum circuit images paired with Braket/Qiskit code) and is author-endorsed via the paper's own load_dataset snippet. GitHub eval-code URLs are hidden for anonymous review in v1, so access is open-data, not open-source. Scope: narrow verified code-generation benchmark, but the index already catalogs comparably narrow scientific code-gen benchmarks (SciCode, CelloAI Benchmarks, ResearchCodeBench), so it clears the bar as category=benchmark, autonomy B.

record.name: Quantum Circuit Vision (QCV)
record.inputs: Quantum circuit diagrams (132 circuits, 13 categories, 1-10 qubits, 5 modalities)
record.outputs: Executable Amazon Braket code verified by unitary fidelity; accuracy and cost metrics per model
record.notes: Cost-aware benchmark testing whether multimodal models can read circuit diagrams and emit verified Braket code; finds circuit depth, not qubit count, predicts failure. QCV-Dataset (MIT) released on Hugging Face; evaluation-code GitHub URLs are anonymized in the v1 preprint, so only the dataset is publicly verifiable.

name: Onnes
reason: arXiv:2607.05805 (v1, 2026-07-07) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('Onnes: A Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Simulator for Cryogenic Fault Diagnosis in Quantum Computing Infrastructure'). Repo github.com/Onnes-Research/onnes verified: exists, MIT license, description and contents (onnesim digital-twin package, 5-role LLM agent panel, evaluation scripts, released run logs) match the paper; the repo URL is given in the arXiv listing itself, so it is author-endorsed. Boundary adjudication (flagged 'system or infrastructure?'): in scope — the index already catalogs quantum-lab infrastructure-operations agents (k-agents A5, Accelerator Assistant A3-A5), and Onnes is the simulation-gated counterpart: a released digital-twin testbed driving a live multi-agent diagnosis loop, validated on real BlueFors logs. Not A5: closure is simulated/log-replayed, no physical actuation.

record.name: Onnes
record.domain: Quantum-computing cryogenic infrastructure operations (dilution-refrigerator fault diagnosis)
record.inputs: Simulated dilution-refrigerator telemetry (physics forward model + noise fingerprints learned from real BlueFors logs); six fault classes
record.outputs: Fault detection and classification with diagnosis rationale; agent-vs-supervised-ML comparison metrics and released run logs
record.notes: Digital-twin simulator driving a live 5-role multi-agent LLM operations layer; few-shot demonstrations plus self-consistency voting lift classification accuracy from 0.685 to 0.990, with 100% recall on physics faults at a 6.4% false-alarm rate on real hardware logs. Closure is simulated/log-replayed (no physical actuation of the fridge); code, data, and run logs released under MIT.

name: PhysMiner
reason: arXiv:2607.04009 (v1, 2026-07-04) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('PhysMiner: An Agentic AI Framework for Discovering Turbulence Physics', Chen/Gao/He, Iowa State aerospace). Paper's availability statement points to github.com/iDesign-Lab/PhysMiner; repo verified: exists, MIT license, and its citation block references this exact paper (arXiv 2607.04009), so ownership is confirmed both directions. Scope: clear multi-step discovery system (discovery agent + validation agent + evolving knowledge library over triple-decomposition CFD analysis), computational closure -> A3, category physics.

record.name: PhysMiner
record.domain: Turbulence / fluid-mechanics discovery from CFD data
record.inputs: CFD flow fields (e.g., OpenFOAM results) plus literature corpus for the knowledge base
record.outputs: Triple-decomposition statistics, visualizations, vortex-line extractions, identified flow mechanisms, and subgrid-scale modeling recommendations with validation reports
record.notes: Agentic framework pairing a physics-discovery agent with a validation agent over triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor; demonstrated on periodic hill flow with improved Reynolds-stress predictions. Source code and the Triple Decomposition Library released under MIT, with a community contribution mechanism for new flow cases.

name: ORBIT-Q
reason: arXiv:2607.03105 (v1, 2026-07-03) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('ORBIT-Q: Dual-axis benchmarking of autonomous agents in scientific quantum programming', Zhang/Chen, CAS Institute of Physics + GSCAEP). Paper's code-availability statement names github.com/sxzgroup/ORBIT-Q; repo verified: exists, Apache-2.0, cites arXiv:2607.03105, contains the 12 containerized tasks, verifiers, and agent harness configs described. Clear in-scope agent benchmark (research-level multi-step quantum workflows, multi-tier verification), distinct from cataloged QMB100/QMP-Bench.

record.name: ORBIT-Q
record.inputs: 12 containerized research-level quantum-workflow tasks across four frameworks (TensorCircuit-NG, PennyLane, MindQuantum, TorchQuantum)
record.outputs: Dual-axis agent-framework co-performance scores via a multi-tier verification pipeline (functional correctness, runtime execution, policy checks, LLM audits, expert review)
record.notes: Harbor-based benchmark varying framework at fixed agent and agent at fixed framework; TensorCircuit-NG scored best among frameworks and Codex+GPT-5.5 among agents, with a substantial gap to expert human implementations remaining. Final verification tier is human expert review. Tasks, verifiers, and evaluation code released under Apache-2.0.
aliases: Open Research Benchmark for Integrated Tasks in Quantum Computing

name: Embodied CAD
reason: arXiv:2606.31252 (v1, 2026-06-30) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('Embodied CAD: Solver-Grounded LLM Agents for Parametric B-Rep Assembly Modeling', Nanjing University). Boundary adjudication (flagged 'in scope if a real system'): it is a real implemented system, not a proposal — FreeCAD-backend execution loop, quantitative evaluation on multi-step mechanical/industrial/mold assembly tasks (100% execution rate with the strong planner; SFT/GRPO-trained weak-planner policies at 93.1% exact accuracy). Index precedent for engineering-design agents under physics exists (CADDesigner, LLM Mechanical Designer). No repository or data links anywhere in the paper -> paper-only. Solver-grounded computational closure -> A3.

record.name: Embodied CAD
record.domain: Engineering design / parametric B-Rep CAD assembly modeling
record.inputs: Natural-language design specifications plus structured parameters
record.outputs: Executed parametric B-Rep assemblies in a FreeCAD backend, with iterative repair/refinement from solver diagnostics
record.notes: Closed-loop LLM agent that iteratively selects skills from a hierarchical L0-L4 library, resolves typed geometric operations, executes in a CAD kernel, and repairs from solver feedback; evaluated on bearing, press-machine, cooling-tower, manifold, and mold-core assembly tasks. No public repo confirmed (none referenced in the v1 preprint).

name: NQS-Agent
reason: arXiv:2606.30464 (v1, 2026-06-29) resolves, not withdrawn; title matches ('NQS-Agent: Health-Aware Agentic Hyperparameter Optimization for Neural-Network Quantum States', Renmin University of China). Boundary adjudication (flagged 'campaign management vs optimization library'): in scope as campaign management — LangGraph-orchestrated agents monitor energy trajectories of running VMC calculations, detect destructive events, stop/modify/resume from checkpoints, and rank candidates, i.e., an autonomous perceive-decide-act loop over a scientific simulation campaign, analogous to cataloged DREAMS and AutoSurrogate (both A3). Access correction: the worklist's 'open-source' claim is not yet true — the paper's code-availability section says github.com/QTMEC-RUC/NQS-Agents 'will be made publicly available on GitHub upon publication' and the URL returned 404 on 2026-08-13, so access is paper-only for now.

record.name: NQS-Agent
record.domain: Quantum many-body simulation (neural-network quantum states / VMC campaign management)
record.inputs: Running NQS/VMC optimization campaigns: energy trajectories, checkpoints, hyperparameter candidates
record.outputs: Intervention decisions (stop/modify/resume from safe checkpoints), adjusted learning-rate schedules, anomaly-aware candidate rankings
record.notes: LangGraph-based agentic campaign manager for NQS hyperparameter optimization, demonstrated on a Heisenberg model where it outperformed baselines and surfaced competitive alternative architectures. Code repository (github.com/QTMEC-RUC/NQS-Agents) is promised 'upon publication' but was not public as of 2026-08-13 (404), so access is paper-only pending release.
